note: The caller-supplied input buffer is stored as the beginning of the parser chunk.
The parser cursor is initialized to the input-controlled chunk contents.
The chunk end pointer is set from the input length, so a two-byte input ending in backslash makes the backslash the last valid byte.
For a quoted key, the opening quote is skipped and the cursor advances to the input-controlled backslash byte.
The quoted-key parser invokes JSON string lexing with chunk->pos pointing at the trailing backslash.
The JSON string lexer copies the input cursor into local pointer p at the final backslash byte.
After seeing a backslash, the lexer advances p without first ensuring that another byte remains for the escaped character.
Because the backslash was the last byte, p now equals chunk->end and this statement reads one byte out of bounds before the later bounds check.
